🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's
response
to a question from
RBC
(RosBusinessConsulting)
on the US deployment of a launcher for intermediate- and shorter-range missiles in Norway
(September 7, 2026)
❓
Question: How does Moscow assess the US deployment of a launcher for intermediate- and shorter-range missiles in Norway, including in the context of the stalled strategic stability dialogue? Is any response planned? If so, what kind?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
We regard the appearance in Europe of US systems capable of launching intermediate- and shorter-range missiles as
yet another step in the endless series of acutely destabilising actions by NATO countries.
In pursuing plans to deploy Western ground-launched intermediate- and shorter-range missiles in the region, NATO not only makes no secret of its intention but
openly flaunts its ambition to acquire a substantial capability to strike deep into Russia’s territory
.
At the same time,
NATO is seeking to bring vast maritime areas of the region within its sights
, establishing dominant control over sea routes of critical military, commercial and transport importance.
In this context, we note that the US missile systems equipped with
Mk 41 launching systems
, which are being brought into Europe and have now been deployed in Norway,
are capable of launching a wide range of missiles against both land and maritime targets
.
☝️
We also take into account that these systems can be used to launch
long-range Tomahawk cruise missiles
, while their deployment in Norway puts
a substantial part of Russia’s European territory, including Moscow, within range
.
Thus, these missile systems could be used in aggressive actions by NATO countries against our country to accomplish
strategic-level objectives
.
Those in Washington and Oslo who made the decision to deploy these systems in Norway should therefore not be surprised that, as part of Russia’s response measures, the deployment sites of the US systems, their command and control facilities, as well as the infrastructure supporting them,
are becoming a particular focus for Russia’s strategic deterrence forces
. This includes planning for the combat employment of the relevant strike assets in the event of an armed conflict.
***
As for the dialogue with the US on strategic stability, we would like to recall that it did not simply “stall”.
It was unilaterally suspended by the Joe Biden administration.
The current US authorities, meanwhile, are
unrealistically discussing the launch of some kind of “multilateral” negotiations with China’s mandatory participation
, even though Beijing has repeatedly and unequivocally stated that it has compelling reasons not to become involved in such work at this stage.
❗️
For our part, we have repeatedly explained in detail that
the conditions for a substantive and productive strategic dialogue with the US are not in place
.
Steps such as the deployment in Europe of US ground-launched intermediate- and shorter-range missiles that threaten Russia will, to put it mildly,
eliminate any basis for a constructive strategic dialogue with the US
.

🇧🇷
On September 7, the Federative Republic of
#Brazil
celebrates
#IndependenceDay
.
#OTD
in 1822, Pedro, the son of Portuguese King João VI, declared — “
Independence or Death!
” — marking the
end of 322 years of Portuguese rule and influence
over Brazil.
The movement for the country’s independence had begun long before that. As early as the late 18th century, revolutionary and national hero
Tiradentes
led a group of like-minded people in Minas Gerais, whose main goal was the
creation of an independent state.
Although the plans of the secret society were uncovered,
Tiradentes became a symbol of resistance
.
As a result of Napoleon’s expansion in Europe in the early 19th century, the independence of the Spanish colonies, and the bourgeois revolution in Portugal in 1820,
the independence movement
in Brazil gained considerable strength
and ultimately led to the proclamation of an
independent Brazilian state
— free from the influence of the Portuguese metropolis.
#Brazil
today is an influential actor of the international community and
one of the world’s leading political and economic powers
. Brasília takes part in addressing many pressing and important issues on the regional and global agenda.
🤝
Diplomatic relations between our countries were established on
October 3, 1828
, although the development of bilateral ties had begun as early as 1811, when
Emperor Alexander I appointed the first Russian consul general in Rio de Janeiro.
Throughout the history of our bilateral relations,
the mutual sympathy of the two peoples
, as well as a genuine interest in each other’s history, culture, and traditions, have remained unchanged. All of this has contributed to the
consolidation of bonds of friendship, mutual understanding,
and mutual respect.
#RussiaBrazil
🇷🇺
🇧🇷
Russian-Brazilian ties are characterized by
strategic partnership
, sustained positive momentum, and an atmosphere of
trust
,
friendship
, and
mutual understanding
. They are based on shared approaches to many issues on the global agenda and a commitment to building a more
just and
#MultipolarWorld
order.
Moscow and Brasília maintain regular contacts at the highest and high levels and
strengthen coordination
in multilateral formats, including at the
#UN
,
#BRICS
, and
#G20
. The two countries promote shared approaches in the field of international security and
cooperate in the maritime sphere.
📈
Positive momentum characterizes
bilateral
trade
and economic cooperation between our countries. Brazil is
Russia’s leading trading partner
in
#LatinAmerica
. For the second consecutive year,
trade turnover
between Russia and Brazil has exceeded $10 billion, with Russia ranking fifth among the largest exporters of goods to Brazil. Particular attention is being paid to expanding and diversifying bilateral trade.
🌟
#Victory81
Russia appreciates Brazil’s careful approach to preserving our shared memory of
the joint struggle of our peoples against Nazism
during
#WW2
. Brazil was the only Latin American country to deploy ground and air forces to Europe to oppose Nazi aggression —
the Brazilian Expeditionary Force made a significant contribution to the common Victory
of the Allies of the Anti-Hitler Coalition over the fascist Reich.
✍️
President of the Russian Federation
Vladimir Putin
in his
congratulatory message
to Brazilian President
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
on the occasion of Brazil's Independence Day
(September 7, 2026):
Relations between Russia and Brazil are successfully developing in the
spirit of strategic partnership.
Our countries
actively cooperate
across a wide range of areas <...>.
There is no doubt that we will continue our constructive joint efforts to
further strengthen
the entire range of mutually beneficial Russian-Brazilian ties. This fully
serves the interests of our friendly peoples
and contributes to the establishment of a new — more just and multipolar — world order.
🎉
We congratulate our Brazilian colleagues and friends on this national holiday. We wish the people of Brazil success, prosperity, and well-being!

item.title: : Government of the Russian Federation On September 7, a ceremony marking the completion of construction of a road bridge across the Tumannaya River, connecting Russia and the DPRK
item.description: Government of the Russian Federation : 🇷🇺 🇰🇵 On September 7, a ceremony marking the completion of construction of a road bridge across the Tumannaya River, connecting Russia and the DPRK, was held on the border between the two countries . The agreement on implementing the project was signed in 2024 in the presence of President of Russia Vladimir Putin and Chairman of the State Affairs Commission of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea Kim Jong-un . Construction began on April 30, 2025 , with Prime Minister of Russia Mikhail Mishustin and Premier of the Cabinet of the DPRK Pak Thae-song giving the official start to the work. 🤝 The construction of the bridge symbolises the commitment to strengthening friendly, good-neighbourly relations and expanding interregional cooperation between Russia and the DPRK . Despite sharing a common border, the two countries previously had no road connection . The capacity of the existing rail route via the Friendship Bridge across the Tumannaya River was insufficient to meet transport needs. The new bridge will provide year-round road traffic . The new route will enable businesses to significantly increase freight volumes and reduce transport costs , while ensuring reliable and stable supplies of various goods. .
The new route will enable businesses to significantly increase freight volumes and reduce transport costs
, while ensuring reliable and stable supplies of various goods. This will contribute to expanding trade and economic cooperation between the two countries.

Russia's Prime Minister
Mikhail Mishustin:
Relations between Russia and the DPRK have today reached an unprecedentedly high level of comprehensive strategic partnership. Our countries are actively cooperating in virtually all areas and coordinating their efforts to ensure regional security and stability.
It is symbolic that the new bridge will bear the name of Red Army officer
Yakov Novichenko
. His feat, accomplished many years ago, resonates with
the unparalleled courage of the Korean heroes
who only recently fought shoulder to shoulder with our servicemen and defended Russian soil.
I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will give a powerful impetus to the further development of trade and economic, scientific and technological, and cultural cooperation between Russia and the DPRK.
ℹ️
The total length of the bridge crossing is
almost 5 km
, while the bridge itself is
around 1 km long
. The bridge has
two traffic lanes
.
More than 70 people
and
over 30 pieces of equipment
were involved in its construction.

item.title: ⚡️ In response to the unfriendly actions of the German side in closing the Consulate General of Russia in Bonn
item.description: ⚡️ In response to the unfriendly actions of the German side in closing the Consulate General of Russia in Bonn and the Russian House of Science and Culture in Berlin , on September 7 the Chargé d’Affaires a.i. of Germany in Moscow was informed of the following retaliatory measures : The Russian Federation is withdrawing its consent to the operation of the Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany in St Petersburg, which must cease its activities no later than September 18, 2026 , with all its staff required to leave Russia by that date. The Goethe-Institut cultural centres in Russia must cease their activities . Their seconded staff have been instructed to leave Russia no later than September 13, 2026 . The head of the diplomatic mission was presented with the relevant notes of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. ❗️ It was stressed that it was the German authorities that once again provoked a new round of escalation in bilateral relations. Full responsibility for the consequences rests entirely with the German Government.

item.title: 🇺🇳 From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council
item.description: 🇺🇳 From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council . The Session is expected to address a broad range of issues on the international human rights agenda, including: • protection and promotion of economic, social and cultural rights, • ensuring the right to development, • protection of children, • combating discrimination against women, • advancing the interests of indigenous peoples, • preventing the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on the enjoyment of human rights, as well as other thematic issues. At Russia’s initiative, a high-level thematic discussion will be held to mark the 60th anniversary of the adoption of the International Covenants on Human Rights . The Council will adopt the outcomes of the Universal Periodic Review of the national reports of Belgium, Denmark, Latvia, Namibia, Niger, Nicaragua, Mozambique, Palau, Paraguay, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Somalia, Sierra Leone and Estonia. 🇺🇳
From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host
the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council
.
The Session
is expected to address
a broad range of issues
on the international human rights agenda, including:
• protection and promotion of economic, social and cultural rights,
• ensuring the right to development,
• protection of children,
• combating discrimination against women,
• advancing the interests of indigenous peoples,
• preventing the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on the enjoyment of human rights, as well as other thematic issues.
At Russia’s initiative, a high-level thematic discussion will be held to mark the
60th anniversary of the adoption of the International Covenants on Human Rights
.
The Council will adopt
the outcomes of the Universal Periodic Review of the national reports
of Belgium, Denmark, Latvia, Namibia, Niger, Nicaragua, Mozambique, Palau, Paraguay, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Somalia, Sierra Leone and Estonia.
At the initiative of the EU, the Council will once again consider
a
politicised and highly confrontational
draft resolution
on the human rights situation in Russia, aimed at extending for another year the mandate of the relevant HRC Special Rapporteur,
Mariana Katzarova
of Bulgaria.
❗️
Russia’s stance on this matter
remains unchanged
: we do not recognise the mandate of this illegitimate special procedure, and any form of interaction with it is unacceptable to us.
The Russian delegation, which will participate in the Session
as an observer
, intends, as before, to make active use of all available opportunities
to overcome confrontation
and
promote a unifying agenda
, as well as
to foster among international partners an understanding of the importance of establishing constructive international dialogue
on the promotion and protection of human rights, with due respect for the national, religious, cultural and historical characteristics of every state.
A number of special side events
will be organised to present Russia’s approaches to the most pressing issues on the session’s agenda to the international community.
